Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all we have from this run-truncated match. Sri Lanka have serious issues with their batting and will have to sort it out before the next game. The third ODI is on 17th October in Pallekele. Do join us at 1430 local (0900 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!

England's skipper and Man of the Match, Eoin Morgan, says it is not a bad start to the series. He feels it was not their best game with the bat as they didn't finish well in the end. States that he and Joe Root have found ways to score on such slow surfaces. Mentions he was very scratchy early in his innings but he was well supported by the batsmen who played around him. Credits the way Sri Lanka, especially Malinga bowled at the death. Appreciates Woakes and Stone for the way they bowled. He believes they can surely do a lot better than today. Tells that they played three spinners and Ben Stokes too was an option but he was not required as they wanted to get the 20 overs bowled quickly.

Sri Lanka's skipper, Dinesh Chandimal, credits England for the way they played. Mentions they failed to capitalize on the start they got with the ball. Admits there were mistakes committed but they showed good enthusiasm out there. He says the batting of Dhananjaya de Silva and Thisara Perera were positives. He feels the total was one they could have chased but the start was not a good one.

After early hiccups, Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Perera managed to bring some sanity in the chase as they stitched in a 43-run stand. This partnership was bettered by the pair of Thisara Perera and de Silva, in which, the former appeared to be in scintillating form. Just when Thisara started to look threatening, the rain picked up its intensity and the umpires were forced to stop the game.

In pursuit, Sri Lanka were pegged back early by the English seamers. Chris Woakes snapped up three wickets and along with Olly Pope, he completely pushed the home team on the back foot. The Lankans lost 4 wickets inside Powerplay 1 and it appeared that the only thing that can save them is the rain. However, England smartly utilized their spinners from both ends to get the 20 overs bowled quickly so that there is no hindrance in their way.

A strong performance by England to go one-nil up in the series. They batted with a lot of control, especially in the first 40 overs, and managed to post a challenging total on the board. Later on, Lasith Malinga turned the clock and produced a magnificent spell to claim a 5-wicket haul. His efforts didn't allow England the kind of finish they desired for in the death overs.
CALLED OFF! We're getting the official confirmation that the second ODI has been called off due to incessant rain. ENGLAND WIN BY 31 RUNS (DLS) and go 1-0 up in the series.
Update 1637 local - The clock is ticking and we have started to lose overs as well. No improvement in conditions as it continues to rain. Signs are ominous. Stay with us for more updates...
Update 1605 local - It's pelting down now and the whole ground is covered. Things not looking too promising currently. We can play until 1800 local time, so let's be positive. Stay tuned.

PLAY STOPPED! The two umpires now come together and now they have decided to call for the covers. It's been drizzling for quite some time and finally, the match officials feel that the conditions are not conducive enough to carry on. Large blue covers are enveloping the entire field as the rain is picking up its intensity. Needless to say, England are well ahead on the DLS par score. Stay tuned for more updates...
A loopy ball on off, Thisara defends it off his front foot.
Full flighted on off, driven off the front foot to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads to deep backward square leg. One run added to the total.
Shortish and on off, Dhananjaya punches from the crease but finds the extra cover fielder.
Goes on the back foot and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Fullish and on off, de Silva tries to flick but gets a soft leading edge to covers.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Presses forward and pushes it to covers.

Confusion but no harm done. Perera flicks it on the leg side and his partner is interested in a run. Thisara initially shows interest but then declines. No harm done as before the fielder gets to it, they are back in their respective crease.
Quicker delivery on middle, worked on the leg side to mid-wicket.

Ben Stokes nearly pulled off a stunner! It will go down as a dropped catch but what an effort! A normal fielder would not have even got a hand to it. This delivery stops a bit onto the batsman after landing around off. Perera stays back to work it on the leg side but gets a leading edge. It loops in the air towards covers, Stokes runs back and puts in a full length dive as he stretches his right hand out. The ball comes in his grasp but Ben fails to hold onto it. Thisara gets a single and a life on this ball.
Spinning into the batsman from off, Dhananjaya goes very deep inside the crease and then punches it to long on for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Goes on the back foot and this time punches it through covers for a run.
Spinning back into the batsman from outside off, on the shorter side, de Silva tries to punch but gets it away from the inner half of the bat. Rolls back to the bowler.
Tossed up ball on middle, turning down, de Silva flicks it off his pads but straight towards short fine leg.
Quicker delivery, on middle and leg, spinning down, Thisara tries to flick but misses. It clips his pads and rolls back.

SIX! Massive hit! Rashid serves a loopy full ball in line of the stumps, Perera clears his front leg and launches it over the bowler's head for a biggie. Hang on folks, this game is not done yet as long as Thisara is there.
Turning away from the southpaw, a bit on the shorter side, Thisara cuts but finds the point fielder.
Gets on the front foot and pushes it with the spin through covers for a single.
Flatter and shorter on off, punched down to long on for a run.
SIX! Welcome into the attack. Rashid tosses it up and lands it wide outside off, Perera gets forward with a big stride, allows the ball to spin back in and muscles it over long on for a biggie.
Adil Rashid to operate now. Game situation - 160 off 150 balls with five wickets remaining.
Tossed up ball on off, Perera gets forward to push at it and gets it away off the outer half of the bat. It goes towards short third man and they cross.

That missed everything! Loopy and full outside off, curling back in, Dhananjaya plants his front foot forward and tries to flick. But it turns back in to beat the inside edge and Buttler fails to collect it. They cross for a bye as the ball rolls towards short fine leg.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven once again but not in the gap at covers.
Beauty! Drifting into the batsman and spinning away after landing, Thisara gets forward to defend but is beaten.
Full floated ball on off, driven through the line but the extra cover fielder made a fine sliding stop. He returned a flat throw to the keeper as Perera was eyeing a run.
Angling into the batsman, on a length, Dhananjaya defends it watchfully from the back foot.
Good length ball angling down towards the leg pole, Thisara glances it through square leg and rotates the strike.
Straighter in line, Thisara taps it down on the leg side and looks for a run but is sent back.
SIX! Perera won't go down without a fight! Stone delivers it short and on middle, Thisara rides the bounce and pulls it with extraordinary force in front of square leg for a maximum.
Back of a length ball on off, it's punched off the back foot but straight in the direction of mid off.
Digs in a short ball on off, Dhananjaya swivels and pulls it in front of square leg for a single.
Pushes it flatter through the air and darts it on middle and leg, Thisara defends it back from the crease.
Full and spinning down the leg side, it's flicked in the air but goes safely in front of square leg for a run.
Shortish and outside off, Dhananjaya moves back and pushes it to covers.
Quicker and shorter this time, around off, Perera punches it to long off for one.
Gets on the front foot and uses his wrists to push it down to long on for another single.
Floated full ball on middle, Perera gets forward and drives it down to long on for a run.
Angles in a length ball on off, Dhananjaya presents a straight bat in defense.
Fighting fire with fire. Another short ball on middle, Thisara is not shying away from the challenge and pulls it to deep square leg for a run.
FOUR! That's hit cleanly. Perera stands back inside the crease, expecting the length to be on the shorter side again, receives one and thumps it over mid-wicket.
Shortish and on middle, Perera goes for the pull but fails to middle it properly. Still, he gets it in the gap past the mid-wicket fielder and a couple of runs results.
A good length delivery on middle, punched from the back foot but straight to mid-wicket.
Beaten for pace! Stone angles across a sharp delivery, on a back of a length and leaving the batsman. Perera tries to punch from the crease but misses.
Starts with a bouncer around leg, Perera ducks and it's called a wide for height.
Olly Stone is back on.
Fires in a shortish ball on off, de Silva hangs back and defends it down safely.
Full and flighted on off, driven through mid off for a run.
Quicker one outside off, punched from the crease to covers this time.
Flatter and shorter on middle, hit across the line but straight to mid-wicket.
Shortish and on middle, punched back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
20 OVERS BOWLED! Now rain cannot spoil this ODI. Shortish and on middle, punched back to the bowler to end the over.
Quicker through the air again, full and on off, Perera keeps it out from the crease to point. A single taken.
Flatter and outside off, punched off the back foot and the extra cover fielder did well to stop the ball.
Jumps out of the crease and drives it through mid off for a run.
Loopy and on off, spinning in, Perera flicks it in front of square leg for a run.
Flighted and full on off, driven through covers for a single.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. Dot ball to end the over. One more over left to constitute a game.
Clips it off his pads to the leg side, it goes through the gap at mid-wicket and takes one.
Loopy and on middle, Perera bunts it down to long on for a run.
Dhananjaya tying his shoe laces. Nice ploy to waste time as it has started to drizzle a bit.
Full and on middle, it's hit down to long on for one.
Tossed up ball on off, defended from the crease to the off side.
Some drops of rain visible now.
Loopy full ball on middle, Thisara drives it down through mid on for a run.

Here comes the first official Drinks break. England are all over Sri Lanka like a rash. They have already removed the cream of Lanka's batting and are just five wickets away from a convincing win. Chris Woakes did all the damage up front while Olly Stone impressed one and all with his ferocious pace. The hosts are reeling, let's see for how long they can fight...
Bowls it with a quicker-arm action and delivers it short around off, Perera punches it down to long on for a run.
Gets on the front foot and flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Tickles it off his pads in front of square leg for a run.
Flatter and on middle, it's pushed back firmly towards the bowler.
Full and on middle, eased it down through mid on for a run.
England are rushing through their overs. Dawson with another one here. Bowls it flat and on middle, it's defended back to the bowler.
On middle, forced on the leg side for a run.
Allows the ball to spin back in and then punches it past the diving mid-wicket fielder for a single.
FOUR! Not the ideal length by Moeen. Keeps it short and around middle, Dhananjaya gets back in and pulls it with the spin through backward square leg.
Fires in a shorter one on off, Perera stands back and taps it down to point for a run.
Quicker and on off, punched down the ground to long off for a run.
Flighted delivery on middle, paddled down fine for a couple.
The players are enjoying a Drinks break now. Seems an unofficial one. Thisara Perera is the new batsman. 205 needed off 204 balls with just 5 wickets left.

OUT! Poor delivery, deserved to be pulled, it's pulled but straight to the only fielder inside the ring on the leg side. A disappointed Kusal departs and Sri Lanka continue to slip badly in this run chase. Dawson is really lucky with this wicket. Perera fails to get his weight entirely on the back foot as he attempts to unfurl his pull shot. As a result, there is no elevation and Roy takes the simplest of catches at mid-wicket. England are roaring!
Shortish and on off, punched to long off for one.
Flatter and on off, defended back to the bowler.
Very full and on middle, de Silva digs it out to mid off.
SIX! High and handsome! Dawson serves a long hop on middle, de Silva picks the length early, goes deep inside the crease and pummels it over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Shortish and on off, punched from the crease to covers.
Dark clouds are surrounding the stadium. The floodlights are switched on. We need 5 more overs in this innings to constitute a game. Let's keep our fingers crossed.
A nice looking paddle sweep. Plays it with the spin and it runs down to fine leg for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Wide! Spinning down the leg side, de Silva fails to flick it and it's a good take by Buttler.
Shortish again, on off, Kusal forces it down to long off for one.

FOUR! Kusal Perera is turning on the heat. A short ball again by Moeen, it's around off and spinning away, Perera camps back and slaps it through covers. Stokes misfields inside the ring and after that there's no stopping it.
Flighted and full on off, defended off the front foot.
Shortish and on off, stroked from the crease to sweeper cover for a brace.
Tossed up ball outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Turns it off his pads to backward square leg and will only get a run this time.
FOUR! Pulled away! Dawson bowls it short and on middle, Kusal moves back to get on top of the bounce and hammer-pulls it behind square leg for a boundary.
Once again a batsman has used his feet. Dhananjaya eases it down to long off for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Uses his feet to get down the track and pushes it to long on for one.
Flatter and quicker outside off, Dhananjaya dabs it down to short third man.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes on the back foot and punches it down to long off for a run.
FOUR! Top edge but safe! Flighted ball around off, Perera top edges his attempted sweep shot and it loops over square leg. The fine leg fielder runs across to his right but fails to reach in time.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Drags his length back and bowls it on middle, de Silva turns it on the leg side, straight to mid-wicket.
Flighted and outside off, driven off the front foot to mid off. End of a good tidy over.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Not out! The impact is umpire's call. Review not lost for England. Coming to the delivery, it's an arm ball around off, straightening a shade after landing. Dhananjaya steps down the track and then tries to defend it with his bat and pad together. Fails to put bat on ball, he's hit on the front pad and they appeal. The umpire shakes his head and Eoin Morgan takes the review after consulting his bowler. The replays confirm about the impact thing.
Shout for an lbw. Not given. Eoin Morgan looks at his bowler and then takes the DRS. Impact seems to be an issue...
Flatter and shorter on off, punched through covers for a single.
A touch short and around off, it's played on the leg side.
Perera has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
This one holds its line outside off, de Silva plays for the spin and gets beaten.
Tossed up delivery around middle and leg, flicked off the pads but straight to square leg.
Quicker and shorter on off, punched down off the back foot to long off for one.

Aerial but safe! Moeen gets this one to skid in with some extra bounce, Kusal is on the back foot trying to dead with it. Probably his idea was to flick but ends up playing it with a straight bat and it takes the shoulder of the bat. The ball loops in the air but falls safely in front of the charging cover fielder.
Fuller and on off, driven off the front foot but straight to the cover fielder.
FOUR! Well played! Signs of aggression by Perera. Moeen delivers it full and around middle, skidding down, Perera brings out the reverse sweep and nails it wide of backward point for a boundary.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled! Now a maximum of 4 fielders can be placed outside the ring till the 40th over. Also Moeen Ali is into the attack.
On middle, fired in at 92 kph, kept out.
Eases it down to long on for a run.
Shortish and outside off, Perera punches it to covers.
Flicks it with the angle towards mid-wicket and for another single.
Slower through the air on middle, Perera flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter around off, Perera pushes it back to the bowler.
Spin introduced! Liam Dawson is into the attack.
FOUR! Top shot to get off the mark! Slightly fuller and on middle, Dhananjaya times it, right off the middle and through mid on for a boundary.
Dhananjaya de Silva is the new man in.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Woakes is breathing fire out there as he gets his third. Once again it is the outswinger which does the trick. Back of a length around off, it shapes away. Shanaka tries to defend from the crease but does not account for the outward movement. The ball takes the outside edge and goes into the gloves of Buttler. He takes it and appeals and the umpire raises his finger. The move to promote Shanaka up the order does not work. England need another 6 wickets to go one up in the series.
Opens the face of the bat and guides it through backward point for a run.
Good length again around off, Perera pushes it to covers.
Fuller in length on off, Perera drives it but not with a lot of timing towards mid off.
Attacks a length and bowls it on the stumps, it is kept out.

Short ball on middle, Shanaka pulls it through square leg, not with a lot of power. Stokes gives it a chase from square leg and keeps it down to two. Poor running by the Lankans, that should have been three.
Good length around off, the batsman punches it firmly towards mid off.
Another back of a length delivery outside off, Shanaka hangs his bat out and the ball beats the outside edge. That was a shot he could have avoided.
Goes a touch fuller this time around off, the batsman defends it to mid on.
Good length again around off, the batsman defends it out.
JAFFA! He has really impressed! Back of a length and at a good pace. It straightens. Shanaka plays inside the line and the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Fuller in length on off, the batsman times it to mid off.
Good length on middle, Perera defends it to mid on.
Nicely worked towards fine leg for a run. They need a partnership here.
Outswing again outside off, left alone.
WIDE! Full and wide outside off, Shanaka goes after it but misses.
Good length on off, blocked.
Good movement! Something we did not see when Sri Lanka were bowling. Back of a length outside off, it pitches and then shapes away. Shanaka plays inside the line and lets it be.
A bouncer and Perera ducks under it. The umpire feels it is fine and that is the over.
Good length again around off, Dasun plays it with soft hands, wide of backward point for a run.
Back of a length on off, the batsman defends it towards point.
Errs in line and bowls it on the pads, Perera tickles it towards fine leg for a run.
WOW! What a delivery, Perera is very fortunate that was not on the stumps. A yorker at 145 kph, just outside off. KP is beaten for pace as he tries to jam it out.
Good length around off, Perera tries to drive it on the up but the ball hits the higher portion and goes towards covers. Bounce and pace, this guy has got everything.
A little too wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Almost another one! On a length around off, Dasun tries to defend but he gets an inside edge past the leg stump and into the fine leg fence. A lucky escape.
Dasun Shanaka is the new batsman at number 5, interestingly ahead of Dhananjaya de Silva. Maybe, sent up to make use of the field restriction.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! No. 3 down and the batsman who would have probably anchored the innings is walking back. A back of a length delivery outside off, Chandimal tries to punch it through the off side by standing tall. But he gets an inside edge onto the stumps. Woakes gets his second and the target now looks an uphill task.
Length again and this one pitches and shapes in. Chandimal tries to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads. England seamers getting good movement here.
On a length and around off, Chandimal pushes it to mid off.
Couple! On the pads, Chandimal flicks it through backward square leg. The fine leg fielder runs to his left and keeps it down to two.
Another back of a length ball outside off, Perera tries to punch but gets an inside edge onto his pads. A successful over for Stone comes to an end.
Good length again on middle, Perera gets behind the line and keeps it out.
Back of a length again on off, Perera defends it onto the ground.
On a length around middle, Perera works it around the corner and the batsmen take two.
Another brute of a delivery! Short again on the body of the batsman. Perera tries to defend but is hit on the body. Even on these dry wickets Olly is getting the ball to zip off the surface.
Kusal Perera walks into bat.

OUT! In the air... taken! Olly Stone gets his first ODI wicket. A snorter to get it. A bumper and it's right on the helmet of Dickwella. He tries to fend it away but the ball takes the gloves and lobs behind to Buttler who takes a dolly. Stone is pumped up and both the openers are back in the hut for Sri Lanka. They are in trouble here.
Attacks the off pole now and Chandimal blocks it. So just a boundary from the over.

Well bowled and well played! Woakes first angles it into the batsman and then gets it to leave him. Chandimal first thinks of playing at it but then seeing the away movement, pulls his bat out in time.

FOUR! Chandimal is off the mark with a boundary! Just need to beat the fielders in the inner ring here and then there is no stopping that. Back of a length and width is on offer outside off. Chandimal punches it through covers and the ball races away.
On the shorter side again, Chandimal punches it to mid off.
Back of a length on off, Chandimal off the back foot pushes it to covers.
On a length around off, left alone.

Once again the batsman is beaten for pace. Stone angles it into the Chandimal. He tries to keep it out but gets hit on the thigh pad. The ball rolls down to third man and a leg bye is taken. A good first over by Stone.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad. The fielding side are asking the question. The umpire isn't interested in the appeal.
Shortish and outside off, the batsman lets it be.
On the pads, Dickwella tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards fine leg and the batsmen run a leg bye.

Beats the inside edge this time. What a beauty! Comes running in and bowls it at a good pace around off, it pitches and then jags back in, cutting Dickwella into half as he tries to defend. Good start by Stone.
WIDE! Down the leg side, Dickwella tries to flick but misses. It has been wided.
BEATEN! A gem to start with! On a length and around off, it angles away. Dickwella tries to defend but gets beaten.
Dinesh Chandimal, the skipper, is the new main in. He needs to lead from the front. Also, Olly Stone to bowl with the second new ball.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! The last ball though ruins it for the hosts. Top nut to receive first up. Tharanga bags a golden duck and just like their opposition, Sri Lanka lose a wicket in the first over. Woakes lands it on a length around off, it pitches and then shapes away. Tharanga tries to defend but the ball kisses the outside edge and goes into the mitts of the keeper. Early strike for England and that ends an eventful opening over.
Takes a single by guiding it down to third man. Already a good first over for Lanka.
Good length around off, Dickwella pushes it to covers.

FOUR! How brave was that? First over and the third ball he faces, he goes for the paddle. Connects and it goes over the keeper and into the fence. Back-to-back boundaries and Dickwella has come out with intent.
FOUR! Off the mark in style! This outfield is lightning quick. On the pads, Dickwella just flicks it through square leg and the fine leg fielder had no chance.
Starts off with a good length delivery around off, angles across the batsman. Dickwella shuffles across and keeps it out.

We are back for the chase! It promises to be an exciting one. The Lankan openers, Niroshan Dickwella and Upul Tharanga walk out to the middle. The former will be on strike and Chris Woakes will open the bowling for England. Here we go...
